h1: The 7 Best Printers With Automatic Document Feeders of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers With ADF 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven printers with automatic document feeders for home offices, from budget Canon units to laser and EcoTank models.
summary: The Canon MF753Cdw II is the best printer with an automatic document feeder: a 35 ppm duplex color laser with a three-year warranty. The Epson ET-4950 is the low-ink-cost pick, and the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e adds duplex at a mid-range price. The ET-4800 is the entry tank, and the Canon TR4720 is the cheapest feeder.
intro: Printers get picked for speed and ink price, and then the weekly routine turns out to be scanning a stack of pages by lifting the lid and feeding them one at a time. An automatic document feeder ends that chore. It only helps, though, if the rest of the machine suits how you work, and a feeder bolted onto a slow, ink-hungry body can still disappoint.

We reviewed seven all-in-ones that list an automatic document feeder on the spec sheet and ranked them on feeder usefulness, duplex support, running cost, connectivity and fit for a home office. We left out any model whose feeder we could not confirm from the listing. Duplex printing is listed for some, but duplex scanning is not stated for any.

products.name: Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II Duplex Laser Printer with ADF
products.verdict: The only laser here, and the one built for a steady daily paper load.
products.description:
The Canon MF753Cdw II pairs an automatic document feeder with a color laser engine that prints duplex at 35 pages per minute, plus copy, scan, fax, wireless and a three-year limited warranty. Laser output keeps its edge on stacks of plain paper, and a feeder that matches the print speed lets you finish a document batch in minutes.

It ranks first because it is the only laser in the group, built for a steady paper load. The Epson tanks cost far less to run but print at 18 ppm.

Buy it for a home office with weekly stacks to print and scan. The caveats are the highest upfront price here and toner that costs more than tank ink. Skip it if you print only a handful of pages a month.
cons: Toner costs more than tank ink
products.idealFor: Home offices with weekly stacks of documents to print and scan.
products.skipIf: You print only a handful of pages a month.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4950 Wireless Supertank Printer with ADF
products.verdict: Refillable tanks turn a feeder printer into a low-running-cost workhorse.
products.description:
The Epson ET-4950 offers an automatic document feeder, refillable ink tanks with up to three years of ink, a 2.4 inch color touchscreen and an 18 ppm print speed. Tanks make the feeder cheap to use all year, because scanning is free and printing draws on bottled ink.

It ranks second because it prints slower than the Canon laser and costs more upfront than cartridge models. It beats the ET-4800 on the touchscreen and ink supply.

Buy it for steady home-office work where cartridge prices irritate you. Skip it if you print rarely, because unused ink dries in the print head over time. For heavy daily output, the laser Canon above is faster.
pros: Up to three years of ink
products.idealFor: Steady home-office users who hate buying cartridges.
products.skipIf: You print rarely and the ink would dry out unused.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One with ADF
products.verdict: A feeder and duplex printing at a mid-range price, with an ink subscription option.
products.description:
The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e combines an automatic document feeder with duplex printing, a three-month Instant Ink trial, wireless setup and a home-office design, in the $50 to $100 range. Duplex printing halves paper use on long documents, and the feeder handles stacks of scans.

It ranks third because cartridge ink adds up, and the subscription option comes with terms. It costs far less up front than the Canon laser.

Buy it for a home office that duplex prints and scans regularly. Skip it if you want the lowest long-term ink cost. Read the Instant Ink terms before enrolling, since billing can continue after the trial.
products.idealFor: Home offices that duplex print and scan regularly.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest long-term ink cost.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless Supertank Printer with ADF
products.verdict: Cartridge-free printing and a feeder at a lower entry price than the ET-4950.
products.description:
The Epson ET-4800 gives a cartridge-free supertank ink system, an automatic document feeder, scan, copy and fax, plus Ethernet and wireless, in a compact body at a lower entry price. Wired networking helps a shared desk stay stable under load.

It ranks fourth because it is an older design than the ET-4950, with no touchscreen noted. In return it costs less.

Buy it for a budget-minded office that wants tank ink and a feeder. Skip it if you want a touchscreen and the latest model. The fax is a leftover feature, but it is handy for occasional paperwork.
products.idealFor: Budget-minded offices that want tank ink and a feeder.
products.skipIf: You want a touchscreen and the latest model.

products.award: Best for Photos and Smart Home
products.name: Canon PIXMA TR8620a All-in-One Printer with ADF
products.verdict: A feeder printer that also handles photos and works with Alexa.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA TR8620a handles print, copy, scan and fax with an automatic document feeder, works with AirPrint, Android and Alexa, and prints photos as well as documents. Phones can print without drivers, and voice control adds a smart-home touch.

It ranks fifth because cartridge ink costs add up and it is not built for heavy volume. It mixes photos and documents, which the laser and tank models do not emphasize.

Buy it for a household that prints photos and scans documents. Skip it if you only print text and want the lowest page cost. For heavier loads, an Epson tank saves money.
products.idealFor: Households mixing photo printing with document scanning.
products.skipIf: You only print text and want lowest page cost.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 Wireless All-in-One with ADF
products.verdict: Feeder and duplex at a mid-range price, with the same core features as the 8125e.
products.description:
The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 shares its core with the 8125e: an automatic document feeder, automatic duplex, a three-month Instant Ink trial, wireless and a home-office design, in the $100 to $200 bracket. It is a near twin.

It ranks sixth because it is near-identical to the 8125e and cartridge ink costs add up. The price difference is the only reason to consider it.

Buy it for a budget-aware home office that wants an HP feeder printer. Skip it if you want the lowest ink cost per page. If the two prices are close, pick whichever is cheaper.
products.idealFor: Budget-aware home offices wanting an HP feeder printer.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest ink cost per page.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer with ADF
products.verdict: The cheapest route to a feeder, sized for occasional multi-page scanning.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA TR4720 is a compact all-in-one with an automatic document feeder for standard paper, print, scan, copy and fax functions, wireless and mobile printing. It is the cheapest route to a feeder.

It ranks last because it is a light-duty machine and cartridge ink costs add up. It trails everything above it on volume, but wins on price.

Buy it for occasional multi-page scanning on a tight budget. Skip it if you scan or print every day. A feeder at this price is useful for a ten-page contract, not a hundred-page archive.
products.idealFor: Occasional scanners on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You scan or print every day.

methodology.description: Automatic two-sided printing earned credit because it halves paper use for document-heavy offices.

whatMatters.detail: An automatic document feeder pulls a stack of pages through the scanner without you lifting the lid for each one. It matters because scanning a ten-page contract by hand is slow and error-prone. Check the listing bullets for the words automatic document feeder, not just scanner. Every model ranked here lists one, which is why they made the cut.

Duplex means the printer prints on both sides of the page automatically. It saves paper and makes reports look professional. Confirm it is automatic duplex, since some listings mean manual flipping. The Canon MF753Cdw II and the HP OfficeJet Pro models list it, while the Epson tanks and PIXMA models here do not highlight it, so check before you rely on two-sided output.

Cartridge, tank and toner systems differ sharply in cost per page. Tank printers like the Epson EcoTank models cost more upfront but save on refills for steady users. Check whether the listing says refillable tank or cartridge before you buy, and consider how much you really print each week before choosing, since that figure drives the payback time.

Rated pages per minute tells you how long a stack takes. A 35 PPM laser clears a long report far faster than an 18 PPM inkjet. Look for the PPM figure in the specs, and remember it measures black text, not photos. The Canon MF753Cdw II lists 35 ppm and the ET-4950 18, which is roughly half the pace.

Wireless is standard, but Ethernet helps a shared desk stay reliable. Mobile standards like AirPrint let phones print without drivers. Look for the exact protocols in the listing, not just the word wireless. The ET-4800 lists Ethernet, and the TR8620a lists AirPrint, Android and Alexa, so match the protocol to the devices you use.

howToChoose.intro: Volume decides which machine pays back its price.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Laser uses toner fused by heat, so it prints fast and does not clog when idle. The Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is the laser pick here.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Inkjet is cheaper upfront and better for photos, but ink can dry out if unused. The Epson EcoTank ET-4950, HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e and Canon PIXMA TR8620a are inkjets.

howToChoose.note: Most home offices should default to inkjet unless they print daily, in which case the Canon laser is worth the jump.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact body, a feeder, wireless, and ideally Ethernet if more than one person prints.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Epson EcoTank ET-4800 is compact for a supertank and offers Ethernet, while the Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the smallest budget option.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print or scan daily. The Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II and Epson EcoTank ET-4950 pay back their price in speed and ink savings.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You scan occasionally. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 gives you the feeder at the lowest cost here.

faq.q: Do all-in-one printers with a feeder also scan double-sided pages?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The listings here confirm a feeder and, for the HP models, duplex printing, but they do not state duplex scanning. Check the specific model's scanner specs before relying on it, because single-sided scanning means flipping stacks by hand.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying a feeder printer?
faq.a: Assuming every all-in-one has a feeder. Many only have a flatbed glass. Always find the words automatic document feeder in the listing before you order, and ignore vague wording such as scanner or multifunction.

faq.q: Is an EcoTank worth it over a cartridge printer?
faq.a: If you print steadily, yes, because refillable tanks cut ink spend. If you print rarely, the higher upfront cost may never pay back, and unused ink can dry out. The ET-4950 and ET-4800 are the tank options here.

faq.q: How do I set up a wireless feeder printer?
faq.a: Connect it to your Wi-Fi from the printer screen or companion app, then add it on your computer or phone. AirPrint and Android printing work without extra drivers on supported models, such as the PIXMA TR8620a and TR4720.

faq.q: Do I need to maintain the feeder?
faq.a: Wipe the feeder rollers and scanner glass occasionally to avoid streaks and jams. Use standard paper and avoid stapled or curled pages in the feeder, which jam most. Dust is the quiet cause of faint lines.

faq.q: Can I use a feeder printer for fax?
faq.a: Several picks list fax, including the Canon and Epson models. You will still need a phone line and should check the model's fax details first, since the feature is a legacy extra.

finalTake: The Canon MF753Cdw II is the right feeder printer for a home office with a steady paper load, thanks to laser speed and a long warranty. Pick the Epson ET-4950 to cut ink costs and the HP 8125e for duplex on a mid budget. Confirm the feeder and duplex in the listing, not the title.
